scenes.say: Ever wondered why interviewers push for composition instead of inheritance? Let’s break down why it matters.

scenes.label: Flexible
scenes.sub: Composition lets you combine objects for flexible designs and easier changes.
scenes.say: With composition, you build classes by combining objects. This keeps your design flexible and makes changes less painful.
Inheritance creates rigid hierarchies and tight coupling. Composition lets you mix behaviors, keeping things loosely connected and easier to test.
Here, a car class uses an engine object. This is composition—no inheritance needed, just combining parts.

scenes.question: When should you use inheritance?
scenes.right: Only when there’s a clear 'is-a' relationship, like car and vehicle. Otherwise, prefer composition.
scenes.say: Don’t use inheritance just for code reuse. Stick to it only when there’s a clear is-a relationship. Otherwise, composition wins.
